answer: Start with the clock. Each identity registers one quartz oscillator and locks a bond of 50 POA times the square of its funder's registered count: 50, 200, 5,000 and 500,000 POA for the 1st, 2nd, 10th and 100th — 100 fakes cost 16,917,500 POA. Each epoch the network pings each oscillator via ocean-fiber beacons and logs its drift in ppm; no two crystals drift alike, so identities sharing one clock file identical curves and merge into one share. Caught clusters forfeit bonds; auditors proving a match collect nectar, 20% of the slash. One fake: 50 POA; a hundred: a fortune for one sip.
